data.title: Zinc pyrithione shampoo (1–2%)
data.summary: X Hair & scalp agents · Organometallic antifungal/antibacterial (zinc complex of pyrithione)
data.body:
_Topicals · X Hair & scalp agents_

**Class:** Organometallic antifungal/antibacterial (zinc complex of pyrithione)

## Mechanism of action
- Pyrithione disrupts fungal membrane transport and causes copper influx → damages iron–sulfur proteins in Malassezia
- Also antibacterial and mildly keratolytic/antiproliferative (cytostatic to keratinocytes)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis of scalp (common OTC shampoos)
- Pityriasis versicolor (as body wash), scalp psoriasis (mild, adjunct)

## Dose & formulations
- Lather onto wet scalp, leave 3–5 min, rinse; 2–3 times weekly, then weekly

## Adverse effects
- Scalp irritation; rare contact dermatitis
- Banned in cosmetics in the EU since 2022 (reproductive toxicity classification) — still used elsewhere

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; broken scalp

## Pregnancy & lactation
Considered safe for short-contact shampoo use (but see EU regulatory status).

## Viva points
- Most common anti-dandruff agent worldwide
- Acts via copper influx toxic to Malassezia

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.51 (Therapeutic shampoos); Khopkar ch.28. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
